2026-05-09T19:02:05.1918634Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1920665Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1922348Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.

2026-05-09T19:02:05.1923693Z

2026-05-09T19:02:05.1929536Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1929890Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1930200Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1930670Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1931051Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1931517Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1945375Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1947202Z >
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1947977Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1948727Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1948923Z ### How to Use
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1949156Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1949679Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1950372Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1950525Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1950910Z # Discover what tools a server provides
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1951421Z <server-name> --help
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1951668Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1952027Z # Get detailed help for a specific tool (type, required status, description)
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1952998Z <server-name> <tool-name> --help
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1953307Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1953661Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1954328Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1954899Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1955078Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1955315Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1955793Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1956282Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1957061Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1957866Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1958581Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1958767Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1959084Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs):
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1959652Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1960157Z safeoutputs --help                                 # list all safe-output tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1961017Z safeoutputs add_comment --help                     # show types and required params
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1961887Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1962990Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1963176Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1963502Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1964059Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1964530Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1965370Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1966028Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1966203Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1966439Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1966841Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1968402Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1970006Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1970161Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1970551Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1971368Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1972410Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1972714Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1973167Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1974239Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1976563Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1977022Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1977208Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1977956Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1978867Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1979026Z ```bash
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1979672Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1980566Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1981228Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1981642Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1982017Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1983025Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1983543Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1983725Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1983907Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1984678Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1985607Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1986528Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1987481Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1988378Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1988882Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1989028Z ### Notes
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1989216Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1989814Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1991171Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1992562Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1993804Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1994983Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1996063Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1996975Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1997755Z </mcp-clis>
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1998155Z <github-context>
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1998704Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.1999388Z - **actor**: agorischek

2026-05-09T19:02:05.2009684Z # Weekly Real-World Testing
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2010061Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2010754Z Run DollarLint against a fresh, bounded set of public repositories, persist the structured result, and publish a Discussion report.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2011618Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2011782Z ## Workflow
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2011977Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2012376Z 1. Use the `dollarlint-repo` MCP server first.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2013107Z    - Call `real_world_history` to inspect `reports/real-world-results.json`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2014205Z    - Use it to avoid repositories that have already been tested unless the manual input explicitly asks for a rerun.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2014940Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2015096Z 2. Choose the corpus.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2016026Z    - If `CANDIDATE_REPOS` is a non-empty JSON array, parse it as the candidate pool. Each item should have `name`, `ecosystem`, and `cloneURL`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2017228Z    - Otherwise use this default pool, skipping anything already in history:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2017752Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2017893Z ```json
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2018218Z [
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2018852Z   {"name":"gitea","ecosystem":"Go/TypeScript","cloneURL":"https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2019931Z   {"name":"vite","ecosystem":"TypeScript/Node","cloneURL":"https://github.com/vitejs/vite.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2021052Z   {"name":"prettier","ecosystem":"JavaScript/Node","cloneURL":"https://github.com/prettier/prettier.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2022314Z   {"name":"fastapi","ecosystem":"Python","cloneURL":"https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2023395Z   {"name":"ansible","ecosystem":"Python/YAML","cloneURL":"https://github.com/ansible/ansible.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2024423Z   {"name":"neovim","ecosystem":"C/Lua","cloneURL":"https://github.com/neovim/neovim.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2025431Z   {"name":"deno","ecosystem":"Rust/TypeScript","cloneURL":"https://github.com/denoland/deno.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2026534Z   {"name":"grafana","ecosystem":"Go/TypeScript","cloneURL":"https://github.com/grafana/grafana.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2027618Z   {"name":"pnpm","ecosystem":"TypeScript/Node","cloneURL":"https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2028832Z   {"name":"huggingface-transformers","ecosystem":"Python","cloneURL":"https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2030025Z   {"name":"node","ecosystem":"C++/JavaScript","cloneURL":"https://github.com/nodejs/node.git"},
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2031105Z   {"name":"kibana","ecosystem":"TypeScript/Node","cloneURL":"https://github.com/elastic/kibana.git"}
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2031884Z ]
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2032358Z ```
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2032539Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2033033Z    - Select up to `MAX_REPOS` repositories. Prefer a small, diverse set over a huge one. Default to 5.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2034378Z    - If the default pool is exhausted, pick other well-known public repositories with distinct ecosystems and conventional config files.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2035271Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2035431Z 3. Prepare and run.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2035911Z    - Call `real_world_prepare_corpus` with `clone: true`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2036776Z    - If it reports duplicates, choose replacements unless this was an intentional manual rerun.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2037971Z    - Call `real_world_run_corpus` with the prepared `corpusDir`, `cacheDir`, and `outputArtifact`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2039551Z    - Nonzero validation exit code 1 is expected when real issues are found. Treat crashes, missing output JSON, hangs, and unexplained warnings as higher-severity product signals.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2040695Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2040874Z 4. Triage the output.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2041372Z    - Inspect the DollarLint JSON output artifact with `jq`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2042529Z    - Separate parsing, validation, schema, coverage, warnings, crashes, performance, and output-contract findings.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2044306Z    - Decide whether each finding is a real third-party issue, expected test fixture data, SchemaStore mismatch, parser compatibility gap, confusing output/reporting problem, or DollarLint bug.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2046730Z    - Summarize product recommendations before finishing the run. Each recommendation must include a strength label of `high`, `med`, or `low`, based on frequency, severity, reproducibility, and expected user impact.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2048022Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2048206Z 5. Persist repository memory.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2049650Z    - Call `real_world_record_result` with the title, corpus, cache directory, command, output artifact, repositories, findings, product recommendations with strength labels in `productDecisions`, and follow-up notes.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2051523Z    - Also append a factual narrative entry to `reports/REAL-WORLD-TESTS.md` using the existing report shape.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2053351Z    - If files changed, request a pull request through the configured `create-pull-request` safe output. Keep the PR title concise and mention the structured result file.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2054414Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2054580Z 6. Publish the report.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2055252Z    - Request one GitHub Discussion through the configured `create-discussion` safe output.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2056287Z    - Title: use the run date and a short result summary, for example `2026-05-09 - 5 repo corpus`.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2057050Z    - Body style:
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2057449Z      - Use `###` and `####` headings only.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2058453Z      - Keep the summary, result counts, notable findings, and product recommendations with `high`/`med`/`low` strength labels visible.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2059645Z      - Put verbose per-file details and raw warnings inside `<details>` blocks.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2060671Z      - Include the tested repository table, DollarLint commit, output artifact path, and workflow run URL.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2062213Z    - If Discussion creation is unavailable, the safe output may fall back to an issue; mention that the intended destination was a Discussion.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2063122Z 
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2064071Z Do not fabricate results. If cloning or validation fails before a meaningful corpus run, publish a short failure report with the blocker, partial artifacts, and the next concrete fix.
2026-05-09T19:02:05.2065202Z
